gloss: on the board; on the game board

definitions.gloss: on the board; on the game board; the board (as a playing field)
definitions.explanation: Refers to the surface of a game board in chess, shogi, go, or similar board games. Used both literally (the physical board) and figuratively (the strategic situation in a game).

examples.japanese: {盤上|ばんじょう}の{駒|こま}を{動|うご}かす。
examples.english: To move a piece on the board.

examples.japanese: {盤上|ばんじょう}の{形勢|けいせい}は{白|しろ}が{有利|ゆうり}だ。
examples.english: The position on the board favors white.

examples.japanese: プロ{棋士|きし}は{盤上|ばんじょう}で{何十手|なんじゅって}も{先|さき}を{読|よ}むことができる。
examples.english: Professional shogi players can read dozens of moves ahead on the board.

notes:
Composed of {盤|ばん} (board, as in {碁盤|ごばん} or {将棋盤|しょうぎばん}) and {上|じょう} (on, above). Primarily used in the context of board games — especially {将棋|しょうぎ} (shogi) and {囲碁|いご} (go) — but also applicable to chess and other tabletop strategy games.

In Japanese culture, shogi and go have deep traditions, and {盤上|ばんじょう} carries a sense of intellectual battle and strategic depth. The phrase {盤上|ばんじょう}の{勝負|しょうぶ} (a contest on the board) can also be used metaphorically for any cerebral competition.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {盤上|ばんじょう}の{勝負|しょうぶ}: a match on the board; a battle of wits
- {盤上|ばんじょう}の{形勢|けいせい}: the position/situation on the board
- {盤上|ばんじょう}を{支配|しはい}する: to dominate the board
- {盤上|ばんじょう}ゲーム: board game

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {碁盤|ごばん}: go board — the physical board itself
- {将棋盤|しょうぎばん}: shogi board — the physical board itself
- {局面|きょくめん}: game position; phase — the state of play at a given moment
